On the coastal sand plain, a wall usually earns its keep holding a level building pad or stopping a sandy face from ravelling - limestone block, quarried locally, is the material most Perth walls are built from. Up on the Darling Scarp, in suburbs like Kalamunda and Roleystone, the ground itself is the driver: steeper slopes, shallow soil over rock, and drainage that has to work through a wet Perth winter. Whichever situation describes your block, the right retaining wall - limestone, post-and-panel, besser block, timber sleeper, rock or boulder - is a decision worth getting right, and the WA permit rules are worth getting right too. See our privacy policy . Common Questions About Retaining Walls Perth Wa Projects How much does a retaining wall cost in Perth? Most Perth retaining walls run roughly $250-$600 per square metre of wall face installed, depending on material, height and access. Limestone and timber sleeper sit toward the lower end for smaller garden walls; taller engineered walls with structural design and permit costs sit higher. These figures exclude GST, excavation, drainage and difficult access - your referred contractor provides a written fixed-price quote. Do I need council approval for a retaining wall in WA? In Western Australia, a retaining wall generally needs a building permit once it retains more than 0.5 metres of ground. A wall of any height can still need a permit if it is tied to other building work, affects or protects adjoining land, or sits on a boundary wall or substantial dividing fence. Always confirm with your local government before starting work. What is the best retaining wall material for Perth's sandy soil? Limestone is Perth's most common retaining wall material, since it is quarried locally and suits the sandy Swan Coastal Plain well. Post-and-panel concrete systems suit taller or longer runs, and timber sleeper works well for low garden terracing. The right choice depends on wall height, budget and whether your block sits on sand, limestone-close-to-surface ground, or the clay-prone alluvial flats around the Swan Valley. How high can a retaining wall be without a permit in WA? The statewide exemption in Building Regulations 2012 (WA) applies only to a wall retaining no more than 0.5 metres of ground, and only when it is not associated with other building work, does not affect adjoining land, and is not on a boundary or dividing-fence wall. Some local councils apply this test strictly, so confirm with your council before assuming a wall under 0.5 m is automatically exempt.
